title: Codility Interview vs Outsourced Interviewing
text:
Codility Interview vs outsourced interviewing: why a platform beats a service
An interviewer for an hour, or a system that compounds
Outsourced interviewing gives you a contractor and a set of private notes. Codility Interview gives you a platform you own: the same evaluation model on every candidate, a full transcript instead of secondhand feedback, and new capability landing on a schedule you don’t control or pay for again.
What a services contract can’t give you
64-71%
win rate when an engineering champion is in the deal
82.6%
Interview adoption where the platform is already live
platform capabilities shipped to Interview since March 2026, at no new cost
An hour of someone’s time is not a system
Outsourced interviewing solves the hour in front of you. It does not solve the interview after that, or the one next quarter, or the one your compliance team asks about eighteen months from now.
Outsourced interviewing service
What you’re actually buying
A contractor’s judgment for a single session, not a repeatable method
Private notes and a summary, not a transcript your team can review
An interviewer’s own AI use on their side of the call, invisible to you
Capability fixed at the terms of the contract, renewed on the vendor’s cycle
Codility Interview
What you own instead
One evaluation model, the same rubric and environment for every candidate, every interviewer
A full transcript, playback, and rubric score your team can review, not a contractor’s recall
The AI Assistant, Claude Code and Codex on or off for each interview, with every candidate interaction captured as reviewable AI activity
New capability ships into the same platform, on the same login, at no new procurement
What breaks when someone else runs the room
None of this is a knock on the individual contractor. It’s what happens structurally when the interview lives outside a system your team controls.
Every contractor is a different rubric
Two interviewers, two judgment calls, two different bars for the same role. Nothing forces the evaluation to be the same twice, because the evaluation lives in the interviewer’s head, not in a shared system.
The record is a summary, not the session
A written recap tells you what the interviewer decided to write down. It does not show you how the candidate debugged, what they tried first, or how they reasoned through a tradeoff.
Capability doesn’t compound
A services contract delivers the same interview format this year that it delivered last year. There is no new environment, no new integration, no new capability arriving because the vendor doesn’t build a platform. They staff a call.
Platform vs service, side by side
Same job: evaluate a candidate’s technical work. Different foundations for what you’re left holding afterward.
Evaluation model
Set by whichever contractor is on the call that day
One rubric and environment, applied the same way every session
Session record
A contractor’s private notes and a written summary
Full transcript, playback, and rubric scores the moment the session ends
Environment
Whatever the contractor’s tooling supports, often a generic live coding tool
Shared VS Code with terminal, sidecar services, and a built-in whiteboard
AI activity
Invisible. The contractor’s own AI use on their end is not something you can see or review
Who’s in the room
A contractor the candidate will likely never work with
Your own hiring managers and engineers, running the interview themselves
Capability over time
Fixed at contract terms. New capability means renegotiating the contract
New capability ships into the same platform and login. No new procurement to get it
Compliance posture
Depends on one contractor’s documentation habits
Structured evidence by default: transcript, integrity signals, rubric, in one reviewable record
A platform keeps shipping. A services contract doesn’t
This is not a roadmap slide. These are capabilities that have landed in Codility Interview since March 2026, at no new cost and no new procurement, for accounts already on the platform.
May 2026
Excalidraw whiteboard in the interview surface
System design discussion happens in the same session as the code, on Codility’s own domain. No IT whitelisting request to get it approved.
Reusable interview environments
Save a configured VS Code interview environment as a library task. Build the environment once, run it across every interviewer and every candidate after that.
Screen-to-Interview solution carryover
Live for every account. The candidate’s Screen work carries forward into the Interview session, removing a manual handoff step between stages.
June 2026
Next.js and R added to the environment library
The task library grows without a new contract. Your interviewers get languages and frameworks your actual stack uses, not a fixed list negotiated a year ago.
One complete downloadable record
The PDF report was rebuilt into a single faithful record: VS Code solutions, integrity and proctoring summaries, code health, AI transcripts, skills evaluations, and the whiteboard, together.
One session, one record you own
A contractor hands your talent team a summary. Codility Interview hands them structured evidence, ready the moment the session ends, without a follow-up email to chase.
Full transcript
Session playback
Rubric scores
Reviewable AI activity
Integrity signals
Whiteboard capture
Immediate, not secondhand
The record comes from the session itself, not from what a contractor chose to remember and write down afterward.
Your team, not a stranger
Candidates interview with the people they would actually work with. Technical judgment and working style are both visible, live.
Defensible when questioned
Transcript, playback, and integrity signals in one place, ready for any hiring decision that needs review.
One evaluation model
The same rubric and environment on every candidate, so a hiring decision doesn’t come down to which contractor was on the call.
An interviewer’s AI use is invisible. A platform makes it reviewable
Where Codility Interview stands today
The AI Assistant, Claude Code and Codex are on or off for each interview, with every candidate interaction captured as reviewable AI activity. Model-level controls are on the roadmap. This applies to the candidate’s side of the session. It also draws a sharp contrast with the alternative: when an outsourced interviewer uses AI on their end of the call, whether to generate follow-up questions, evaluate an answer, or draft feedback, that use happens outside your system entirely. There is nothing to review, because there is no record to review it in.

What we hear from teams evaluating this
Our outsourced interviewer is good, and our hiring managers trust them
That trust rests on one person’s judgment, applied a different way in every session they run that week. A platform doesn’t replace a good interviewer’s instincts. It gives every interviewer, including your own hiring managers, the same environment and rubric to work from, and a transcript afterward so that trust doesn’t depend on memory.
We don’t have engineering bandwidth to run interviews ourselves
Codility Interview is built for your own hiring managers and engineers to run the session, in a real VS Code environment with sidecar services and a whiteboard, not a generic live coding tool bolted onto a video call. The time cost is the interview itself, the same hour you’re already paying a contractor for. What changes is who owns the record afterward.
How do we know the platform will still be relevant in two years?
Look at what shipped in the last four months alone: a built-in whiteboard, reusable interview environments, Screen-to-Interview carryover, new languages and frameworks, and a rebuilt complete session record. That is the argument for a platform over a service. The contract you sign today gets more capable without a new negotiation.
